html:
In 1783 the king of Spain issued the Cedula of Population, offering land in Trinidad to Catholic settlers from friendly nations. Spain had held the island since the 1500s but had done little with it.

Settlers poured in from the French islands, especially Martinique and Grenada, bringing enslaved Africans. Free people of colour received land too, though less than whites. In a few years the population grew many times over and sugar and cocoa estates spread.

Trinidad became French in speech and custom while Spanish in law. A British force took it in 1797, and it was ceded to Britain in 1802. French Creole culture shaped its Catholic church and its Carnival.
